problems.form_value: The paper says participants were randomly assigned; both members of a dyad share one condition, and every analysis is at the dyad level.
problems.source_says: Minor. Not every analysis is at the dyad level. The S1 homogenization test is a Wilcoxon test on idea-level cosine distances to each condition's average idea embedding, pooled across dyads, and the form itself codes that outcome (S1-O4) with unit 'output'. Sec. 4.1.4 also says the entropy gives 'each idea's topic diversity score'. The REML models, the noticing-rate test, and the correlations use one value per dyad. Suggested wording: 'the REML analyses use one score per dyad, and the homogenization test compares idea-level distances.'
problems.quote: we conducted a Wilcoxon test on the Access-to-Cue factor, comparing the cosine similarity between each idea and the average embedding of all ideas within each condition (See Appendix A.4.1).
problems.locator: PDF p. 11 (printed p. 306), Sec. 6.3, first paragraph; PDF p. 16 (printed p. 311), App. A.4.1; PDF p. 7 (printed p. 302), Sec. 4.1.4

problems.form_value: 'Cue arms received a GPT-4o-mini cue about once a minute; NoCue arms received none.' how_used describes only the ideation-task prompt (App. A.3.2).
problems.source_says: Minor omission, not an error. Appendix A.3 gives a separate GPT prompt for familiarity-building cues and says the prompts were used. Every dyad did the familiarity-building task before the ideation task 'to help participants get acclimated to the system'. The main text counts cues only for the 20-minute ideation conversation and does not say whether Cue dyads also got cues during the warm-up (the N=10 pilot ran both tasks). The form could record that the Cue treatment may have started in the familiarity-building task.
problems.quote: We provide the prompts that we used to generate the (i) familiarity building (ii) ideation and (iii) wikipedia entity based cues below.

The pre-survey served 'balancing across conditions', and 'Conditions were balanced for gender (M=42, F=127, Non-Binary=3) and age', but only pooled totals are printed. confirmed.statement: Check (d): the comparison arm matches the form (no AI, ai_vs_bau). 'In the Cue conditions, cues were provided (3.2.2), whereas in the NoCue conditions, no cues were given.' All dyads were briefed on the call frame, the collaborative notes, and the task prompt, and only the notification mechanism was specific to the cue condition. Sec. 4.1.2's 'Every group got approximately one cue per minute' must mean cued groups, given Sec. 4.1.1.

The four arm descriptions match the text: Virtual partners in separate rooms and InPerson partners in one room (Sec. 4.1.1, Fig. 3), the researcher in the call frame or in the room (Sec. 4.1.2), the call window inactive in person (Fig. 2 note), and a visual notification and chime with each cue (Sec. 3.2.3, Fig. 2). arms[].ai = generative_ai for the Cue arms and none for the NoCue arms is right.

summary: The PDF states three times that the 172 participants were randomly assigned to a 2 x 2 between-subjects design that crossed GPT-4o-mini conversational cues (about one a minute) with meeting modality, and the NoCue dyads used the same interface without cues, so random assignment to generative-AI assistance versus none holds (PDF p. 5, Secs. 4 and 4.1.1; PDF p. 11, Sec. 8). The coding is refuted only in detail: what_was_assigned says every analysis is at the dyad level although the homogenization test compares idea-level distances, the form does not mention that the appendix gives a prompt for familiarity-building cues that Cue dyads may also have received, and the source note that the markdown lacks the appendix is stale.
